With edge 0->2 absent, cutting 0->1 starves both intermediate nodes, collapsing every path except 0->3.
Adding a residual skip where none existed gives a large optimization gain, while replacing an existing conv with skip trades away capacity.

Upgrading the weak parameter-free pooling on the final 2->3 edge to a 3x3 conv adds the most useful capacity.

Swapping a 3x3 conv for avg pooling on 0->2 removes learnable capacity, unlike swapping a none or skip edge.
When 2->3 is missing, a conv on 1->3 becomes one of the few learnable paths into the output, so it gains much more.
Replacing pooling on the first edge with a 3x3 conv lets every downstream path through node 1 learn features, giving a larger gain than replacing a 1x1 conv.
